items.quote:
What happens when a wealthy society forgets the boundary between the two and attempts to institutionalize unscoped, unconditional kindness as the public policy toward every anonymous stranger? Because anonymous bureaucracies cannot personally verify who is a genuine crisis case and who is a criminal or a habitual dependent, unscoped public "kindness" becomes an **invitation to systematic abuse**. Opportunists convert temporary emergency provisions into permanent support, and criminals interpret the refusal to enforce public order as license to plunder.

Conversely, a household that practices only cold *politeness* inside the home treats its own children like strangers. Keep the rule clear: Dispositional goodwill and politeness toward all; costly action-based love and kindness budgeted by tier, anchored at home where personal knowledge can supervise and form character.
items.problem: Shorter draft as your note on the held draft asks (call:civ/chapters/08_ch08.md:9547789f:note/examples-and-rule): "This is good, but it strays from the main point. We can quickly show one or two situations. Then make the point about kindness. I hesitate with COVID, because the government also forbid going out. Yes, it was rife with fraud. Is there a clearer example of a kind gesture where poitness should have taken its place?" COVID is gone. The first paragraph is the one you called good. The three sourced paragraphs are replaced by one situation, Hurricane Katrina in 2005: the agency paid two thousand dollars on the applicant's word, usually before any inspection, and the Government Accountability Office estimated that about one payment in six, about a billion dollars, rested on an identity, an address, or a claim that was false or filed twice. The agency disputed the size of the estimate and accepted most of the recommendations for checking applicants (GAO-06-844T and GAO-06-1013, 2006). It is a kind gesture given where a fixed rule belonged. (a) That one situation, then the point about kindness and your two closing sentences. (b) A second situation for your sentence on public order: the House of Commons committee on the August 2011 disorder, in its own words. Length: original 124 words; a 342; b 374. Sources are in ext-ref/kindness_politeness/dl_round2/.

alternates.label: one situation
alternates.text:
A wealthy society can forget the boundary between the two and attempt to institutionalize unscoped, unconditional kindness as the public policy toward every anonymous stranger. The attempt fails for a plain reason. An anonymous bureaucracy cannot personally verify who is a genuine crisis case and who is a criminal or a habitual dependent, so unscoped public "kindness" becomes an **invitation to systematic abuse**. Opportunists convert temporary emergency provisions into permanent support, and criminals interpret the refusal to enforce public order as license to plunder.

Hurricane Katrina showed the failure in 2005. The Federal Emergency Management Agency meant to be kind. It paid two thousand dollars, on the applicant's word and usually before any inspection, to each person who reported that the storm had displaced him. The Government Accountability Office then sampled the payments. It estimated that about one payment in six, about a billion dollars, rested on an identity, an address, or a claim that was false or filed twice. One applicant gave a cemetery as the location of a damaged home (GAO-06-844T, 2006). The agency disputed the size of the estimate and accepted most of the recommendations for checking applicants (GAO-06-1013, 2006). The help was needed. Its form was wrong. The agency bore a cost without reckoning it and asked for no proof, which is what kindness does. A household can give that, because it sees the person every day. An agency never sees him.

The rule follows from who can know whom. Kindness restrains abuse only where the giver knows the receiver and can watch his conduct, as the members of a household do. A public agency knows no claimant face to face. Such an agency cannot give kindness. It can give a stranger only a fixed rule applied alike, and that is politeness. Conversely, a household that practices only cold *politeness* inside the home treats its own children like strangers. Keep the rule clear: Dispositional goodwill and politeness toward all; costly action-based love and kindness budgeted by tier, anchored at home where personal knowledge can supervise and form character.
